beats.heading: Week Nine: publishing support
beats.narration_text: This is my Week Nine Humanitarians AI progress report, covering November second through November eighth. I prepared YouTube titles and descriptions for contributor videos and supported the submission process for Sanjana's review. Week Nine is the focus; Week Eight appears later only as a comparison. Liam, narrating for Deepa.

beats.heading: Five contributors. Seventeen videos.
beats.narration_text: Week Nine covered seventeen video submissions from five contributors. Anjana contributed four, Tanmay four, Om four, Mohammed three, and Uday two. These counts describe the work in my supplied account, not publication statistics. Each submission needed a title and description that represented its own content clearly.

beats.heading: The subject must come from the record
beats.narration_text: The subjects in a publishing package need to come from the actual submission. I used available topic and filename information to prepare relevant wording. Earlier projects can provide context, but they do not prove what a contributor submitted in Week Nine. Without a verified topic mapping in this report, I am not assigning earlier project names to these seventeen videos. That keeps the account grounded in the work I can support.

beats.heading: Make each title specific and readable
beats.narration_text: I prepared titles to communicate the subject of each video in concise, readable language. The aim was to help a viewer identify the topic and understand what to expect. A title should reflect the submission rather than make a claim beyond it. This is communication work: selecting relevant wording and maintaining a consistent presentation. It is not evidence that I reviewed source code or modified a contributor's implementation.

beats.heading: Write descriptions that orient viewers
beats.narration_text: For descriptions, I summarized the topic, educational purpose, and key concepts supported by the submission information. I worked on the publishing materials, not the underlying technical projects. The distinction matters: a polished description is useful context, but it does not independently establish technical correctness, approval, or publication. Those outcomes require their own evidence.

beats.heading: Send for review. Keep status clear.
beats.narration_text: The videos and prepared metadata were sent for approval through Sanjana's review workflow. I report that submission step without calling it final publication. Prepared material, a review request, an approval, and a public upload are separate states. Keeping the wording precise helps avoid confusion about what is complete and what still needs a decision.

Submission is not a publishing decision.

beats.heading: A comparison—not an extra count
beats.narration_text: For comparison, Week Eight involved fourteen videos. Week Nine involved seventeen, making thirty one across the two weeks. These are submission counts, not unique contributor counts or published-video totals. Onkar's October nineteenth work belongs to an earlier week and is excluded from both totals.

beats.heading: Clear metadata supports clear review
beats.narration_text: I learned to keep contributor details, topic wording, and review status consistent across multiple submissions. Accurate metadata supports the next decision without pretending that decision has already happened. Humanitarians AI.
